response.sql:
WITH test_ratios AS (
    SELECT p.SEX, 1.0 * l.CPK / l.GPT AS ratio
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL
      AND p.SEX <> ''
      AND l.CPK IS NOT NULL
      AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL
      AND l.GPT <> 0
), group_averages AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
    FROM test_ratios
    GROUP BY SEX
), first_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio
    FROM group_averages
), first_kept AS (
    SELECT g.SEX, g.avg_ratio, m.mean_ratio AS first_mean
    FROM group_averages AS g
    CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m
    WHERE g.avg_ratio > m.mean_ratio
), second_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio
    FROM first_kept
), remaining AS (
    SELECT f.avg_ratio, f.first_mean, m.mean_ratio AS second_mean
    FROM first_kept AS f
    CROSS JOIN second_mean AS m
    WHERE f.avg_ratio > m.mean_ratio
)
SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS average_remaining_group_ratio_averages,
       AVG(avg_ratio - first_mean) AS average_excess_over_first_mean,
       AVG(avg_ratio - second_mean) AS average_excess_over_second_mean
FROM remaining;

assumptions.assumption: A missing ratio means CPK or GPT is NULL, or GPT is zero (which would make the division undefined); these tests are excluded. Ratios and means use ordinary arithmetic averages without rounding.
